title: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’
slides: Microsoft's Nadella just proposed an AI emergency brake. Why now?
Once AI models are deployed, they can be hard to control.
But an emergency brake might not work for all models.
You'll need to demand emergency stops in AI systems you use.
Check if your AI tools have a kill switch. Ask your vendor.
thread_text:
1. AI's Missing Brake

Microsoft's CEO just called for an emergency stop button for AI. But once these models are out, they don't come with a recall switch.

2. Deployment Lock-In

After an AI is live, its behavior can drift or be gamed. Retraining or shutting it down often means rebuilding the whole pipeline.

3. Not All Models Brake

Some AI systems run on edge devices or are open-source. A centralized kill switch can't reach them once they're copied.

4. Your Vendor's Switch

If you use AI tools, you're responsible for knowing if they can be stopped. Ask for documentation on emergency shutdown.

5. Test Your Tools

Pick one AI tool you use today. Ask the vendor: 'How do I kill it instantly?' If they can't answer, switch.

instagram.caption:
Microsoft's CEO now says AI models need an emergency brake. ⚠️

Once an AI is live, its behavior can drift or be gamed, and shutting it down often means rebuilding the whole system.

Some models run on personal devices or are open-source, so one central kill switch can't reach them once they're copied. 🔌

If you use AI tools, you're responsible for knowing whether yours can actually be stopped.

So pick one tool you use today and ask your vendor: how do I kill this instantly? 🛑

If they can't answer, what's your next move? 🤔
